execution_context.trigger: runtime (client-side, when user visits eCommerce site)
execution_context.file_location: Injected JavaScript via third-party plugin (e.g., QuickView plugin) or remote script tag

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code injects a remote JavaScript file from a malicious domain, which then reads payment or credential form fields and exfiltrates the data to an attacker-controlled server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Injecting remote scripts from untrusted or lookalike domains is a common method for web skimming and credential theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal third-party scripts should not access sensitive form fields or exfiltrate data to unknown domains. Loading scripts from domains that closely resemble legitimate services (e.g., Google Analytics) is highly suspicious.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or payment providers may load scripts dynamically, but only from well-known, verified domains.
key_indicators: Script loaded from domain similar to trusted provider (e.g., gocgle-analytics.com)
Access to sensitive form fields (payment, credentials)
Outbound network requests to attacker-controlled domains

attack_chain.action: Attacker compromises a third-party plugin (e.g., QuickView) or registers a lookalike domain (e.g., Gocgle Analytics).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious script is loaded on eCommerce sites.

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript is injected into the client-side environment when a user visits the site.
attack_chain.leads_to: Script executes in the user's browser.

attack_chain.action: Script reads sensitive data from payment or login forms.
Script exfiltrates collected data to attacker-controlled remote domain.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen credentials or payment information (final goal).

behavioral_signatures: Client-side JavaScript making network requests to domains similar to trusted analytics or payment providers
Obfuscated or base64-encoded JavaScript loaded at runtime
Access to sensitive form fields (e.g., credit card, login) by third-party scripts
file_indicators: Injected <script> tags referencing non-standard or lookalike domains
Presence of obfuscated or dynamically created script elements in the DOM
network_indicators: Outbound requests to domains with typosquatting (e.g., gocgle-analytics.com, not google-analytics.com)
Unusual POST requests from client-side scripts to unknown or recently registered domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor client-side script activity for dynamic script injection, especially from domains that closely resemble trusted providers. Use CSP violation reports to detect unauthorized script sources. Analyze network traffic from the browser for outbound requests to suspicious or lookalike domains, and flag scripts that access sensitive form fields or use obfuscation techniques.
